Draw a model, some links or a feature tree

Source: R/plot.R
vp_plot.Rd

Draws what vp_dot() describes: requirements as blue arrows (from the feature that requires to the one required), conflicts as dashed red lines and at-least-one lines as dotted green lines. A minimal form (vp_minimal()) is much easier to read than the complete graphs, which have an arrow for every consequence.

Usage

vp_plot(
  x,
  file = NULL,
  layout = c("dot", "neato", "fdp", "sfdp", "circo", "twopi"),
  engine = c("diagrammer", "graphviz"),
  width = NULL,
  height = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

What to draw; see vp_dot().

file

Where to save the drawing: a file ending in .svg, .pdf or .png. NULL: no file (with engine = "graphviz", a temporary PDF file).

layout

How the nodes are placed: "dot" (layers: best for requirements), "neato" and "fdp" (springs: best for conflicts), "sfdp" (springs, for large graphs; drawn as "fdp" by DiagrammeR), "circo" (a circle) or "twopi" (rings around a centre).

engine

"diagrammer" (the R packages DiagrammeR, DiagrammeRsvg and rsvg) or "graphviz" (the programs of Graphviz).

width, height

The size of the htmlwidget (any CSS size, or a number of pixels); NULL lets it fill the space.

...

More arguments of vp_dot(), such as graphs, features, highlight, fill or rankdir.

Value

Without file and with DiagrammeR, an htmlwidget. With file, the path of the file, invisibly.

Details

By default the drawing is made by the package DiagrammeR, which includes its own copy of Graphviz: nothing needs to be installed outside R. Without file the result is an htmlwidget, which RStudio shows in its viewer and R Markdown puts in the document. With file the drawing is saved; SVG needs the package DiagrammeRsvg, and PDF or PNG also need rsvg. With engine = "graphviz" the drawing is made by the programs of Graphviz, if it is installed (they are looked for in getOption("variplex.graphviz"), the variable GRAPHVIZ, the PATH and the usual folders), and always saved to a file.

See also

vp_dot() for the source of the drawing and the meaning of its arguments.

Other drawing: vp_dot(), vp_dot_compare(), vp_plot_compare()

Examples

band <- vp_generate(vp_example("miband3.uvl"), or_graph = TRUE)
if (requireNamespace("DiagrammeR", quietly = TRUE)) {
  vp_plot(vp_minimal(band))
  vp_plot(vp_minimal(band), graphs = "excludes", layout = "neato")
  vp_plot(vp_feature_tree(band))
}


# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("DiagrammeRsvg", quietly = TRUE)) {
  file <- vp_plot(vp_minimal(band), file = tempfile(fileext = ".svg"))
  file.exists(file)
}
#> [1] TRUE
# }
